findings.title: Countdown and match start count offline retained members, so a match can start with nobody online
findings.problem: The STARTING countdown validates the player count with getPlayerCount(), which is players.size() (membership), not the online player count. When settings.auto-leave-on-quit=false, MultiArenaManager.handleQuit keeps the member's UUID in the arena (keepPosition = !isAutoLeaveOnQuit() || inProgress), so the count never drops when players disconnect. Every other liveness path in this class uses getPlayers() (online only): ensureEmptyArenaTaskRunning, onGameStart's teleport/kit loop, broadcastI18n. The countdown therefore passes its 'enough players' gate with an empty server, setState(RUNNING) fires, onGameStart teleports nobody, and GameManager.startGame() also passes because it compares the same membership set against getArenaMinPlayers() (GameManager#getArenaMinPlayers -> ArenaInstance#getMinPlayers). addPlayer (line 349/382) and isFull() use the same membership count, so an arena full of offline members also rejects real joiners.
findings.impact: With auto-leave-on-quit disabled (a documented setting), a countdown started while members are online keeps running after all of them disconnect; the match starts with zero online players, spawns a full wave and villagers, loses all villagers/nodes unattended, and the settlement path then records a defeat (sessionVictory=false) for every offline member during reset()'s backfill (recordOffline). The arena is unusable for its whole settlement + empty-arena window while producing false loss statistics.
findings.trigger: arenas.yml settings.auto-leave-on-quit=false; two players reach min-players in WAITING/STARTING, both quit (positions retained and pendingRejoins created), countdown reaches zero.

findings.title: Delayed reset is fire-and-forget with no handle or generation guard, so a second reset can wipe a freshly reopened arena
findings.problem: scheduleReset() only flips the resetScheduled boolean and then schedules reset() with runTaskLater without keeping the BukkitTask, so the pending reset cannot be cancelled, identified or superseded. reset() clears resetScheduled at entry (line 1358) while restoreStarted is still true, so a second scheduleReset() during the reset window is accepted and queues another full reset. If that second reset fires after completeResetAfterRestore() has already set restoreStarted=false and state=WAITING, it runs against a reopened, joinable arena: restoreStarted is false, so the early return at line 1355 does not trigger; reset() then sets state=ENDING, calls gameManager.stopGame(), kicks every online member through removePlayer() (teleport to lobby + snapshot restore + stats recorded as a mid-session leaver) and re-runs the map rollback. MultiArenaManager documents this exact hazard for retired arenas ('只排一个延迟任务且不保存句柄'), but the same live-instance path has no generation check.
findings.impact: A player who joined the reopened arena and is waiting in the start countdown is silently ejected to the lobby with their session recorded as a mid-match leave, the countdown is cancelled, and the arena re-enters ENDING/rollback for no reason. Repeated admin stops during the reset window keep re-arming the same stale reset.
findings.trigger: /hilltop stop <arena> (HilltopCommandHandler 'stop' has no state guard) executed while the arena is already in its post-game reset delay or rollback, followed by completeResetAfterRestore() finishing before the newly scheduled delay elapses.

findings.title: getStatus reports READY from map presence, hiding a stuck-ENDING instance and blocking /hilltop enable
findings.problem: getStatus() derives READY purely from activeArenas membership and never looks at the instance's GameState or its restore barrier. An instance stays in activeArenas after a failed or blocked reset, where ArenaInstance.reset() deliberately parks it in ENDING with restoreStarted=false when restoreWithResult is rejected or rollback fails (lines 1430-1446) and logs 'the arena stays in ENDING'. getStatus() still answers READY for that arena. handleEnableArena pre-checks before == ArenaStatus.READY and returns the 'arena-enable-already-ready' message without calling enableArena, so the documented recovery path is not reachable through /hilltop enable, and status displays (ArenaCommand/ArenaAdminService/SetupWizard) show a healthy arena that no player can join (addPlayer rejects everything but WAITING/STARTING).
findings.impact: After a rollback failure the arena is permanently unjoinable but advertised as READY; the enable command refuses to act, so an admin following the log's own advice ('run /hilltop disable ... then /hilltop enable ...') must discover by trial that only disable-then-enable works. Any status surface built on getStatus() (list, manage GUI, reset gate messages) is wrong for the whole outage.
findings.trigger: Arena reset whose map rollback cannot start or finishes with failed blocks (ArenaInstance.reset lines 1425-1446), then /hilltop enable <arena> or any status listing for that arena.

unverified: No build or runtime execution was possible (read-only audit); every conclusion is from static reading of the four slice files plus the call sites needed to establish reachability (HilltopCommandHandler, HilltopVillagePlugin, GameManager, MapRestoreManager, ArenaManager, ArenaResetService).

S04-F1 assumes settings.auto-leave-on-quit=false is configured; with the shipped default (true) a quit during STARTING goes through leaveArena and the count does drop, so the defect is config-gated rather than default-on.

S04-F2's window depends on the rollback duration versus settings.arena-reset-delay; on small journals the rollback finishes inside the delay, on large journals the stale reset fires while restoreStarted is still true and instead leaves resetScheduled=true until completeResetAfterRestore clears it. Both orderings were traced statically; the exact frequency was not measured.

I verified that no arena/MultiArenaManager method in this slice is reachable from an async scheduler callback (the only runTaskAsynchronously call sites are PlayerGoodsManager, StatsManager and CommandsDocumentGenerator, which do not touch these classes), so no async Bukkit-API finding is reported.

MultiArenaManager.stopArena (line 504) leaves statuses at its previous value and has no caller in src/main/java, so the stale-READY variant of that path was dropped as unreachable rather than reported.
notes: The slice is heavily hardened by earlier fix rounds (session ids for the settlement countdown, restoreStarted barrier, rejoin-window/goods-snapshot ordering, retired-world quarantine), so the remaining defects are concentrated in (a) membership-vs-online accounting and (b) reset/status bookkeeping that is not tied to the instance generation. Concurrency here is single-threaded Bukkit main-thread re-entrancy rather than true parallelism: the risky re-entrancy points are synchronous MapRestoreManager completion callbacks inside reset() and the /hilltop stop -> stopGame -> scheduleReset -> reset chain.
